top_opportunities.title: [Bounty: $75] Package hygiene: sideEffects flag, export-map validation, and publint in CI
top_opportunities.description:
**Context**
`package.json` publishes a dual CJS/ESM build (`main`/`module`/`exports`) via tsup, but declares no `sideEffects` field (bundlers must assume the SDK can have side effects and keep more than necessary), and nothing validates that the published artifact's export map, `files`, and types entries are actually coherent. `pnpm build` succeeding does not catch misconfigured `exports` paths or types that don't resolve for `moduleResolution: "node16"` consumers — the class of bug that only surfaces after `npm publish`.

**Proposed Change**
Add `"sideEffects": false` to `package.json` (verify no module-level side effects in `src/` first — the current sources are pure declarations, but confirm). Add `publint` as a devDependency with a `pnpm publint` script, and run it in CI after `pnpm build` (new step in the existing job or its own job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Fix anything publint flags.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- `sideEffects: false` is set, justified by a clean check of module top-levels.
- `pnpm publint` passes locally against the built `dist/`.
- CI runs publint after build and fails on findings.
- No changes to the runtime bundle contents beyond what the flag enables downstream.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Suggested Label**: chore
**Bounty:** $75
**ETA:** 24 hours

top_opportunities.title: [Bounty: $75] Website: accessibility and motion-preference fixes for the landing page
top_opportunities.description:
**Context**
`website/` is the project's landing page with a scripted hero animation (`website/src/hero-animation.ts`, `website/src/animations.ts`). Marketing pages built around canvas/CSS animation commonly ship without `prefers-reduced-motion` handling, keyboard-navigable CTAs, or proper document landmarks — and this page is the first impression for developers evaluating the SDK. Without seeing the rendered page the exact gaps can't be listed exhaustively, so this bounty is scoped to an audit-plus-fix pass rather than a single known bug.

**Proposed Change**
Audit the landing page against WCAG 2.1 AA basics and fix what's found: honor `prefers-reduced-motion` (static fallback for the hero animation), ensure all interactive elements are keyboard-reachable with visible focus states, verify color contrast of body text and CTAs, add meaningful `alt`/`aria` where assets are decorative, and ensure a single logical `h1` with ordered headings. Keep the visual design intact — this is not a redesign.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- Hero animation does not run (or runs a static variant) under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, verified in dev tools.
- Full keyboard pass: tab order reaches every control, focus is always visible.
- Automated check (axe or Lighthouse a11y) reports no critical/serious issues on the page.
- `pnpm --filter website build` (or the website's build command) passes.
- A short summary of fixed issues is included in the PR description.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for the SDK, plus a local website build.

**Suggested Label**: feature
**Bounty:** $75
**ETA:** 48 hours

top_opportunities.title: [Bounty: $60] Docs: add a "Failure modes and recovery" guide
top_opportunities.description:
**Context**
The README documents the happy path well, and `src/errors.ts` has excellent inline rationale — but a integrator debugging a failed mainnet transfer has to assemble the recovery story by reading source. The pieces are scattered: `TransferError.burnTxHash` (recover via `completeMint`), `AttestationNotReadyError` (retryable, burn is safe), `SubmissionTimeoutError` (hash exists, outcome unknown — check the chain before retrying), `IrisRequestError` (Circle-side outage, retry), and `resolveBurn` for inspecting a burn you didn't produce.

**Proposed Change**
Add a `docs/` page (or a major README section, matching wherever long-form docs currently live — check `INTEGRATION.md` first and extend it if that's the right home) covering: the transfer lifecycle diagram in prose, each error class with what it means for funds and what to do next, a worked `completeMint` recovery example for both directions, and guidance on choosing `pollTimeout`. Link the new section from the README's relevant existing sections.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- Every error class exported from `src/index.ts` appears in the guide with meaning + recommended action.
- At least one complete code example: catch `TransferError` → wait → `completeMint`.
- The guide distinguishes "funds are safe, retry" from "outcome unknown, inspect first" cases explicitly.
- Links from README/INTEGRATION.md to the new guide work.
- Docs-only PR; `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` still pass untouched.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Suggested Label**: documentation
**Bounty:** $60
**ETA:** 24 hours

top_opportunities.title: [Bounty: $60] Harden scripts/testnet-smoke.mjs with retries, exit codes, and a step summary
top_opportunities.description:
**Context**
`scripts/testnet-smoke.mjs` is the end-to-end testnet check (`pnpm smoke`) and one of the few signals that the SDK works against live Circle Iris and real contracts. Public testnets and faucets flake constantly — transient RPC 5xx, attestation delays just over the poll window, faucet rate limits. A smoke script with no retry or step-level reporting turns every flake into a false alarm, and a script that doesn't exit non-zero on partial failure turns real breakage into a green-looking run.

**Proposed Change**
Restructure the script into named steps (fund/check, approve+burn, attestation wait, mint) with per-step retry + exponential backoff for infrastructure-shaped failures only (not for deterministic validation failures). Exit non-zero if any step ultimately fails, print a per-step pass/fail/duration summary at the end, and keep the burn hash printed prominently on post-burn failure so a human can recover the run with `completeMint`. No new dependencies — plain Node.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- Each step retries transient failures with backoff; deterministic failures (bad address, insufficient funds) fail immediately without retry.
- Final summary lists every step with status and duration; process exit code reflects overall outcome.
- Post-burn step failure prints the burn hash and the `completeMint` invocation needed to finish.
- Script remains runnable with existing env vars from `.env.example` / README smoke instructions.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (script correctness reviewed manually; live run optional).

**Suggested Label**: chore
**Bounty:** $60
**ETA:** 24 hours

top_opportunities.title: [Bounty: $45] Validate input to bytes32ToStellarAddress
top_opportunities.description:
**Context**
`bytes32ToStellarAddress` in `src/utils/encoding.ts:28-32` does `Buffer.from(hex, "hex")` with no validation and passes the result straight to `StrKey.encodeEd25519PublicKey`. `Buffer.from` silently truncates at the first non-hex character and accepts odd-length strings by dropping the leading nibble, so garbage input produces a garbage-but-plausible `G...` address instead of an error. Its sibling `stellarAddressToBytes32` (lines 12-25) validates both directions of the strkey round trip; this inverse got missed. It's exported from the package via the encoding utilities consumers import.

**Proposed Change**
Mirror the validation discipline of `evmAddressToBytes32` (lines 120-131): require an `0x`-prefixed, even-length, pure-hex string of exactly 64 hex chars (32 bytes) before decoding, and throw a descriptive error otherwise.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- 32-byte valid hex input round-trips: `bytes32ToStellarAddress(stellarAddressToBytes32(g)) === g` for sample G-addresses.
- Non-hex characters, odd lengths, wrong byte lengths, and missing `0x` prefix each throw with a clear message.
- Contract (C...) round-trip behavior is documented — either supported explicitly or rejected explicitly; not silently mangled.
- Tests added in `tests/encoding.test.ts`.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Suggested Label**: bug
**Bounty:** $45
**ETA:** 24 hours

top_opportunities.title: [Bounty: $45] Export convertPrecision and add 6↔7 decimal round-trip tests
top_opportunities.description:
**Context**
`convertPrecision` in `src/utils/encoding.ts:137-147` implements the Arc(6)↔Stellar(7) decimal conversion that sits at the heart of every cross-chain amount in this SDK, but it is not exported from `src/index.ts` — integrators building fee displays or amount inputs against both chains have to reimplement bigint scaling themselves. Meanwhile `parseUsdcAmount`/`formatUsdcAmount` (same file, lines 92-115) and `decimalsForChain` have test files, but there is no dedicated coverage of conversion round trips (up-scale then down-scale, truncation behavior, zero, and max-precision inputs) through the public amount helpers.

**Proposed Change**
Export `convertPrecision` from `src/index.ts` (with its existing doc comment intact). Add tests in `tests/amount.test.ts` (or `tests/encoding.test.ts`, matching where related cases live) covering: 6→7 upscale exactness, 7→6 downscale truncation, identity when decimals match, zero, and round-trip precision loss cases with documented expected values.

**Acceptance Criteria**

- `import { convertPrecision } from "@asctp/parabola"` typechecks against the built entry and is in the export list.
- Round-trip tests pin exact bigint expected values, including at least one truncation case.
- No runtime code changes beyond the re-export line.
- Verified by the `typecheck-test-build` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

**Suggested Label**: feature
**Bounty:** $45
**ETA:** 24 hours

top_opportunities.title: Evaluate one scoped build-bounty pilot against an internal build
top_opportunities.description:
## Outcome

Complete one useful open-source build through the paid-slot system in #2054 and decide whether it saves team effort and produces sufficient product value.

## Pilot sequence

1. Rehearse the complete flow without funds: publication, three claims, a timely submission, missed deadline, rejection, shared award, full winner fee refund, team cancellation/system-fault refund, appeal, and transfer reconciliation.
2. Select a bounded team-defined build with a public interface, reproducible acceptance evidence, named reviewer, documented internal-build estimate, fee and fixed alpha reward pool.
3. Record separate operator authorization for the capped funded pilot, including the approved funding source and wallet configuration. This issue itself is not that authorization.
4. Run one round under the published terms: at most three attempts, five-day default delivery window per paid claim, seven-day review target, human acceptance and manual awards/refunds.
5. Deliver one useful accepted build. Track later integration and production adoption separately; they are not prerequisites for earned awards.
6. Publish a source-safe report comparing usable output, turnaround, reviewer time, integration effort, reward spend, retained/refunded fees, and total operator effort with the internal-build estimate. Record expand/revise/stop and reasons.

## Acceptance
